newsitem.title: USA: Quaker doubles profits despite lower sales due to Snapple.
newsitem.headline: Quaker doubles profits despite lower sales due to Snapple.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co. said Thursday that its profits more than doubled in the latest quarter despite a drop in sales, lower prices for breakfast cereals and heavy spending on its struggling Snapple beverage line.
The giant food company said net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose to $133 million, or 98 cents a share, from $61.5 million, or 45 cents per share.

The company said, however, that the results included a $133.6 million pretax gain on the sale of its frozen foods business, and $23 million in pretax restructuring charges for various U.S. foods and beverage operations.

Excluding these factors, the company said, net income was about $72 million, or 53 cents a share, well above Wall Street estimates of 46 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Investors, however, were not pleased, sending Quaker's stock plunging $1.75 to $34.625 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said third-quarter sales slipped to $1.44 billion from last year's $1.55 billion, which included $72.3 million in sales from divested businesses.
Total beverage sales fell 11 percent to $593.4 million from $664 million while total food sales rose 3 percent to $840.2 million from $817.3 million.

"We had two major financial hurdles to overcome in the quarter, the ready-to-eat cereal price decrease and the marketing investment in Snapple sampling," Chairman William Smithburg said in a statement.

"Thanks to our exceptionally strong hot and ready-to-eat cereal volumes and strong operating margin improvement in Gatorade, as well as in many of our other U.S. and Canadian foods businesses, we were able to overcome these challenges."

Quaker said its beverage sales decrease was due to a 23 percent decline in sales volumes of Snapple juice drinks, lemonades and teas. It said that despite an intensive summer promotional campaign for Snapple products their sales fell 9 percent to $512.6 million from $563.8 million.

"Clearly, the biggest challenge facing the company is Snapple's disappointing performance," Smithburg said. "The integrated sampling and advertising campaign that ended in mid-September generated some excitement behind the brand this summer, but we're still disappointed."
The company said North American foods sales increased 2 percent to $687.3 million from $676.6 million, despite the 15 percent price decrease in ready-to eat cereals.
International foods sales rose 9 percent to $152.9 million from $140.7 million, with increases in Latin America, Europe and the Pacific.
The company said it used the proceeds from its frozen foods divestiture to lower its debt levels, and improve tax and working capital management.

Quaker said that its net income for the first nine months dropped to $229.8 million, or $1.68 a share, from $771.8 million, or $5.75 a share, as sales declined 13 percent to $4.14 billion from $4.77 billion.
